author: /root/sphinx
scope: Typed suspension/automatic continuation, serializer registration, reference-context propagation, recipient/count/collection retention, copy-as-enters tails and delayed riders. Root separately reviews executor/domain semantics; Ferocity separately reviews the fixed14 bank.
findings: New answer/automatic frames retain typed effect, full EffectContext, actual controller, fixed count, legal defenders and remaining recipients. Automatic recipients are registered under both ContinuationFrame and AutomaticContinuation; the defender answer is registered under AnswerContinuation. Legacy constructor defaults preserve old frame shapes.

Both new frame types participate in canonical read/write ObjectReferenceEnvironment propagation. The existing resolution-key restriction remains unchanged, so authorized moves are propagated only to the same resolution. Original contexts, source fields and existing target-resolution rules are retained rather than replaced with unrelated source identity.

The actual answer requires exactly one singleton defender per original token index, validates membership in both the offered list and current legal list, and routes errors through the canonical ActionProcessor atomic rollback. No target-assignment, ward or becomes-target event is introduced by this resolution-time non-targeting choice.

Plain creation evaluates its base count and recipient list once, then prepares the per-recipient count once. Both replacement decisions and defender decisions retain the prepared count and actual recipient. Decline resumes the original prepared batch; accept uses the prepared copy path without recounting.

A recipient tail is pre-pushed even for the final recipient. Synchronous completion pops only that exact tail; paused output is appended to its created-token accumulator, and resumed remaining recipients carry the complete earlier output into the original consumer. This avoids losing the first or last recipient after suspension.

Copy-as-enters retains the exact remaining defender list and all created-token IDs. A zero-remaining automatic frame publishes the final paused token instead of dropping it. Existing source-copy calls remain on their default legacy path. A null entry-choice pause falls through with the original state so its temporary tail/rider state is not duplicated.

Delayed sacrifice/exile riders are registered for only the newly created IDs in each partial copy segment, then carried through serialization. The new prepared attached-copy conversion retains tapped/attacking, original recipient, sacrifice/exile and conditional-turn/Ring-bearer/stamp riders applicable to the original effect. Existing collection propagation and canonical continuation draining preserve outer composite work.

The explicit initialCounters plus attached-copy limitation returns a technical error. It is not turned into successful creation with missing counters. The corresponding frozen-pool membership check is separate and must not be inferred from a pilot policy.
limits: This is source review only. Fixed14+original Dalkovan2 actual receiving artifacts, full CI and the original priority bank remain required.

No complete token implementation, generic replacement ordering, arbitrary changed-visit target history or whole-game acceptance is claimed. Existing target-resolution and direct producer boundaries remain independently subject to receiving qualification.
Manual pre-entry projection added a required beforeEntry argument at the same token entry calls; a receiving merge must preserve both changes through explicit overlap review.

The separate accepted effect-registry entry-snapshot donor does not qualify every paused/direct continuation producer merely by being copied; receiving entry-observation compatibility remains separate.
